interfaces: Actual source: src.load.load_twitch_file(file_path: str | pathlib.Path) -> int, returning aggregate count; TASK.json incorrectly declares -> None. Preserve integer returns and load_data('twitch', path) dispatch, src.main twitch-streams CLI, and transform_twitch_streams(raw_data: dict) -> list[dict]. Each aggregate contains twitch_game_id, twitch_game_name, viewer_count, stream_count and sample_time. parse_twitch_fetched_at returns datetime. insert_twitch_game_snapshot(connection, snapshot) performs an upsert without committing. public.twitch_game_snapshots has UNIQUE(sample_hour, twitch_game_id); inspected migrations show no incoming foreign keys. Existing dbt staging and analytics still consume snapshot_time. Authorized changes are limited to src/load.py, src/transform.py, tests/test_twitch_hour_replacement.py and docs/TWITCH_HOUR_REPLACEMENT.md. This is a proposal for controller approval.
approach: Validate and transform the entire observation before writing. Reject observations producing no game aggregates. Within one ordinary psycopg transaction, acquire LOCK TABLE twitch_game_snapshots IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE, then read the target hour's rows in a separate statement, apply ordering/replay rules, upsert all incoming aggregates using the existing helper, and delete target-hour rows whose game IDs are absent from the incoming set. Commit once; propagate failures so the connection context rolls back all changes. The table lock serializes replacements even when the hour initially has no rows and conflicts with ordinary table writers. This is the smallest conservative locking solution, at the cost of serializing different-hour writes. Upsert plus deletion preserves IDs and snapshot_time for retained games; newly added games retain the existing insertion-clock meaning. Keep unrelated hours, loaders, migrations, downstream interfaces and historical bronze files unchanged. Document the bounded completeness and empty-input policy. Add real PostgreSQL acceptance tests within the authorized new test file.
timestamp_and_completeness_policy: fetched_at is an ISO string written using aware UTC datetime after the extractor's pagination loop completes. The parser converts aware timestamps to naive UTC and currently accepts naive timestamps unchanged; retain compatibility by interpreting naive values as UTC. sample_time is that observation instant; sample_hour is its UTC hour floor. Both database columns are TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE; sample_time remains nullable in the schema. snapshot_time defaults to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and means insertion time. Incoming rows always use sample_time_source='bronze'; historical 'load_clock' values are proxies. Proposed ordering: compare against maximum existing bronze sample_time for the hour. Older input is an explicit no-op returning 0. Equal timestamps with exactly identical complete aggregate contents are a replay returning the aggregate count without writes; different contents at the same timestamp raise ValueError. A strictly newer observation replaces the entire hour. If only load_clock rows exist, accept bronze as authoritative rather than treating proxy clocks as observation times; reject existing bronze rows with missing timestamps. Actual Twitch bronze is flat {source, request, fetched_at, stream_count, data}, not the general body/outcome envelope described in ARCHITECTURE.md. Completeness means the complete configured top-stream sample, not all Twitch streams. Accept nonempty legacy fetched_at/data inputs under that declared contract; validate source/request and integer stream_count against list length when present. Reject explicit failure/incomplete indicators, missing or non-list data and malformed records; preserve legitimate unassigned-stream filtering. Reject every zero-aggregate observation, including data=[], before mutation: without a durable hour watermark, clearing the hour would allow later stale data to return. Neither matching counts nor nonempty data proves upstream pagination completeness; the extractor records no such evidence.
risks: Source provenance cannot be independently verified here: workspace HEAD is db2bb6d19b55ecc06fbcee05faf54918a7306b67 ('Freeze isolated role input'); TASK.json names 0653617666399590c853c39f08e8cf97c9eca45c, which is unavailable as a local Git object. Controller must attest that the frozen files correspond to the intended source.

Rejecting empty observations is a deliberate bounded policy requiring controller approval. Supporting authoritative empty replacements while preserving stale-order protection requires a durable per-hour watermark and expanded schema/file scope.

Historical nonempty bronze has no requested-page count, terminal cursor or completion marker. Compatibility therefore depends on trusting the declared sample contract; malformed or silently truncated successful API responses cannot all be detected by these allowed changes.

The table lock blocks writes for other hours until transaction completion. Reads remain available under PostgreSQL MVCC. Ordering checks must run after lock acquisition under READ COMMITTED; combining lock and state inspection under an older snapshot can invalidate the concurrency argument.

Existing mocked tests in tests/test_load.py assert exact INSERT-only SQL counts and expose no fetchone method. Necessary lock/read/delete statements invalidate those assertions. That file is outside the allowlist; controller must approve updating obsolete tests or explicitly record their incompatibility, rather than adding production branches for test doubles.

Existing mixed observations require conservative ordering against the newest bronze timestamp and complete-content comparison for ties. Historical load_clock timestamps cannot establish real observation order. Direct per-row helper calls do not provide whole-hour replacement semantics.
test_environment: Existing tests/conftest.py provides a separate PostgreSQL database, default steam_analytics_test, built from sql/create_tables.sql plus the full migration chain and dropped afterward. It repoints POSTGRES_DB, refuses equality with the working database, and truncates public data tables before database tests. The db fixture rolls back its own connection, but loader commits occur on separate connections. table_digest supports logical-content checks; existing Twitch digest excludes IDs and snapshot_time. CI supplies PostgreSQL 18 with Python 3.10, runs ruff and pytest, and sets REQUIRE_DB_TESTS=1 so an unreachable server fails rather than skips. Compose exposes PostgreSQL on default port 5433. Proposed acceptance covers initial load, exact replay, membership replacement, failure after at least one write with rollback, independent hours, stale/equal timestamp policies, timezone normalization, historical provenance, invalid/incomplete/empty inputs, and overlapping same-hour loads using separate connections with bounded synchronization. Assert one complete winning observation and no mixture, including initially absent hours. No tests, database connections, credential access or network operations were performed in this read-only architect inspection; infrastructure availability is established from source only.
